newsitem.title: USA: Glickman not tied to meat user fee,must find funds.
newsitem.headline: Glickman not tied to meat user fee,must find funds.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Thursday he is not wedded to the idea of meat and poultry inspection user fees, but said that there must be other resources found to fund increased inspections.

"To be honest, I'm not wedded to the idea of user fees," Glickman told a food policy conference, but said that resources to improve the nation's meat inspection system must be found "within the current budget constraints."
The administration's budget proposed that $400 million be raised through industry user fees for improved food safety inspections. The controversial proposal has been criticized by the industry.
Glickman said he is willing to work with Congress to find another funding option, but said he would not compromise his commitment to improve the U.S. food safety system.
"There are certain basic functions that government has to do well, and food safety is one of those," Glickman said.

Asked if he would be willing to potentially decrease the funding for some government feeding programs to pay for the increased inspections, Glickman said "I don't want to see one traded off for another" and said that lawmakers will ultimately have to make the funding decisions.
